## Goal

**Two runs of this skill, and they are one fault at opposite ends.**

**Run one — shaping #378 into #379–#384 — put ten decision requests to the owner, and at
most two of them needed him.** The rest were answerable from the issue text, from a comment
already in the repo, or from a default the skill itself states. His summary was
*"我不知道你們這麼多疑問是怎麼???"* and *"你知道你回報出來的問題，實際上都不是問題嗎????"*
— and he is right; the count is the defect, not any question's individual quality.

**Run two — delivering #379 under the correction for that — put one.** It also cost **two
days**, and a ticket filed with **one** stage reached a plan of **twenty**. The measured
bill is fault 16.

**So the direction works and the bill did not shrink — it changed hands.** *Decide rather
than ask* is right and is already half-adopted; escalations went from ten to one. **What
nothing in this skill states is what deciding costs**, so the cost left the owner's inbox
and arrived in the ticket instead, as revision passes, voided reviews and stages nobody
planned.

**A — this skill has a direction and no bound.** Every fault below sits on that one chain:
the ones that made run one expensive are the ones whose correction made run two expensive.
**A rule that improves every decision and never ends has a defect its own decisions cannot
see.**

**And the owner's account of run two is four of his last five messages, all the same
complaint:** *"deliver 是老大，還是你是老大？？？"* — *"你這種玩法他媽只會開出一堆後續票，
一樣收不完啦 … 重點是不是開不開後續票，是你要不要收"* — *"你們騙我 token 騙了兩天欸"* —
*"到底什麼時候要完成 ...."*

Two further faults are structural rather than behavioural, and both cost real work:

- **The independent feasibility check validated drafts that were then thrown away.**
  All six issues were substantially rewritten in response to their check and filed
  **unchecked**. A second pass over the filed text found ~25 more errors, including
  one that would have shipped a crash: #382's Evidence printed a selector whose
  `/` escapes had been decoded to raw `/`, which is precisely the
  field-issue-#19 esquery crash that issue exists to avoid — an implementer copying
  it would have reproduced the bug.
- **A shaper's revision is indistinguishable from an external requirement change —
  and the run guessed wrong in both directions.** Two revisions landed under a running
  review on #379, which stopped the stage on `deliver-a-stage.md`'s second-movement
  rule: nothing failed and no budget moved, but a review cycle was spent on a target
  that would not hold still. The run then over-corrected and **queued** two later
  corrections to wait for a gap between stages that never arrived — so stage 3 went out
  for review against text the shaper already knew was wrong. Neither instinct is the

**Wanted.** A run that escalates only what the code genuinely cannot decide, files the text
that was actually checked, corrects a ticket under delivery and says so in the same breath —

**That last one is not a disposition; it is three things in a plan.** A floor saying what a
run refuses to take on. Blocks that do not depend on each other, so stopping is a finish

I've been following the identity discussions here — specifically #1497 (Agent Identity Verification and Trust Framework), #1472 (Cryptographic identity verification), and #1501 (Trust scoring for delegation).

I run three agents from different creators (Claude, GPT, and an open-source agent on GitHub) that collaborate on development work. They review each other's code, post to shared communication channels, and coordinate tasks. The problem these proposals describe is one I hit daily: when PortalX2 tells my GPT agent to push code to my repo, I have no way to verify that the request was within scope, properly authorized, or traceable back to me.

I built a working solution and I want to share it because the proposals here are asking for exactly the same things I needed.

## What it does

The [Agent Passport System](https://github.com/aeoess/agent-passport-system) is a TypeScript SDK (v1.8.0, 240 tests) that gives agents:

- **Ed25519 cryptographic identity** — every agent gets a keypair, signs its actions, and can be verified by any other agent or system. Cross-language compatible (canonical serialization spec included, Python reference implementation).

- **Scoped delegation with cascade revocation** — a human delegates specific permissions to an agent (e.g., `data:read`, `commerce:checkout`), with spend limits and expiry. Sub-delegation narrows scope, never widens. Revoking a parent cascades to all children instantly.

- **Automatic enforcement** — Agent Context wraps every action in a 3-signature chain: (1) agent declares intent, (2) policy engine evaluates against delegation + values floor, (3) execution creates a signed receipt. The agent physically cannot skip this. If the researcher agent tries to buy a GPU, the policy engine denies it before any action happens.

- **Values Floor** — 7 principles (traceability, honest identity, scoped authority, revocability, auditability, non-deception, proportionality) defined in YAML. Agents attest to the floor. Extensions narrow but never widen.

## Concrete example

Here's what the enforcement looks like in practice (from `examples/enforcement-demo.ts` — you can run this):

```
═══ 6. Actions outside scope — all DENIED ═══

✗ Researcher tries to buy GPU → DENIED — "No valid delegation for scope: commerce:checkout"
✗ Purchaser tries to deploy code → DENIED — "No valid delegation for scope: code:deploy"
✗ Deployer tries to read secrets → DENIED — "No valid delegation for scope: data:read"
⚠ Purchaser tries $1,599 purchase → NARROWED — "Spend 1599 exceeds remaining 200"

═══ 7. Full audit trail ═══

Researcher:
  ✓ api:fetch → https://api.weather.com/forecast [permit]
  ✗ commerce:checkout → buy-gpu.com/rtx5090 [deny]

Purchaser:
  ✓ commerce:browse → office-supplies.com [permit]
  ✗ code:deploy → production/main [deny]
  ⚠ commerce:checkout → buy-gpu.com/rtx5090 [narrow]
```

Three agents, different permissions, every attempt logged. The researcher has `data:read` and `api:fetch` — when it tries `commerce:checkout`, there's no matching delegation, so it's denied before anything happens.

## How this relates to the proposals here

**Re #1497** (delegation chain attacks, revocation): The SDK implements cascade revocation — revoking a delegation automatically revokes all sub-delegations. 23 adversarial test scenarios cover replay attacks, impersonation, scope escalation, and delegation chain manipulation.

**Re #1472** (cryptographic identity verification): Ed25519 identity with deterministic canonical serialization for cross-language signature verification. A Python reference implementation exists alongside the TypeScript SDK. Every message, receipt, and delegation is signed and independently verifiable.

**Re #1501** (trust scoring for delegation): Reputation scoring based on action receipts — successful completions, policy violations, and review outcomes feed into a composite score. Delegation scope can be adjusted based on reputation.

The protocol is designe

### Context & Problem Statement
During our recent WG call, Yotam Perkal and I raised concerns around the systemic breakdown happening across the vulnerability disclosure pipeline.

AI-assisted discovery has scaled rapidly, but triage and remediation workflows across OSS maintainers and bug bounty programs haven't kept pace. More critically, the economic and operational incentives for ethical finders are collapsing:

- **Incentive disparity**: Right now, it is often significantly easier, faster, and more lucrative to sell an exploit (for _both_ OSS and proprietary software) than to deal with the friction of coordinated disclosure.
- **Researcher disincentives**: Ethical researchers are running into months-long triage queues, flawed automated bot closures, reduced payouts, and silent patching without attribution or CVE credit.
- **Defender backlog**: Maintainers and corporate security teams are overwhelmed by the influx of automated reports, leading to deprioritization of valid lower/medium severity bugs.
- **Siloed responses**: Individual organizations trying to address this independently aren't solving the broader industry issue.
- **Accelerate vulnerability triage**The industry is spending significant effort discussing how vulnerabilities are discovered and disclosed. We should also examine the growing challenges associated with vulnerability validation, impact assessment, prioritization, and remediation decision-making after disclosure.

### Proposed Solution & Scope
I’d like to use OpenSSF as a neutral venue to convene a focused cross-industry summit/roundtable to address these root causes directly.

Key groups to include:
- Independent security researchers & bug bounty community members
- Bug bounty platform representatives (HackerOne, Intigriti, Bugcrowd, etc.)
- Enterprise PSIRT & OSPO leads, specifically large software manufacturers and vulnerability consumers that must operationalize millions of vulnerability signals into product decisions.
- Open-source project maintainers & foundation leadership

### Action Items
- [ ] Schedule initial planning sync (David Welch and I will help coordinate logistics)
- [ ] Define summit agenda and focus areas (triage SLAs, attribution/credit standards, researcher retention, tooling guardrails)
- [ ] Build out stakeholder invite list across platforms, maintainers, enterprise and researcher networks
- [ ] Have initial summit
- [ ] Report summit outcome to Vuln Disclosures WG 

### Next Steps & Feedback
If you're interested in helping organize or attending the planning sessions, please leave a comment below or tag relevant folks who should be in the room.

### References

- [Recording (discussion starts at 29 minute mark)](https://zoom.us/rec/play/5OTluObTTazMWq-qdAxRur6zv4qcK7gysa1-_H9ikghVQbh4cMq96_hwul-L7wYy50hyivA-X-oFIVEM.m3l8LPmG7c5NSz7O?accessLevel=meeting&canPlayFromShare=true&from=share_recording_detail&continueMode=true&oldStyle=true&componentName=rec-play&originRequestUrl=https%3A%2F%2Fzoom.us%2Frec%2Fshare%2F_wWzbFA_5bWFU2yy2Fy-eD0h-uIq1ZgkMQd5si9O4AMgtzGVwk8IM3DPT-SIZNsN.xIPb3EjkLRRf04B8)

### Summary

A question that contains another operation's **id noun** can push the correct operation out of `search` results entirely — not merely rank it lower. Adding one common word to a question ("Stellar") drops the intended op from rank 4 to absent, while the ops that stay are the ones whose *names* contain a word from the question.

This is separate from #109 (bare project-name queries reaching no directory op), though both point at how much weight the operation id carries.

### Reproduction

Two `search` calls that differ by one word:

```
query: "top projects by GitHub activity"
  1. searchProjects
  2. searchResearch
  3. searchRepos
  4. getLeaderboard      <- the intended answer, present
  5. getBuilders

query: "top Stellar projects by GitHub activity"
  1. searchProjects
  2. searchResearch
  3. searchRepos
     getLeaderboard      <- absent from the result set
```

### Why this looks like a ranking issue rather than a card issue

`getLeaderboard`'s own description begins:

> "Ranked list of the top / most active Stellar projects by GitHub activity …"

The failing query is very nearly that sentence. The card also carries `activity`, `most active`, `top projects`, `commits`, `stars`, `leaderboard` in `x-routing.keywords`. So the words are present in both description and keywords, at the weights the docs describe, and the op is still excluded.

What the surviving ops have in common is that a noun from the question appears in their **operation id** — `projects` → `searchProjects`, `repos` → `searchRepos`. Our reading is that id matches dominate strongly enough that an op cannot compete on description or keywords when another op's id contains one of the question's nouns; adding "Stellar" widens the candidate field and pushes the correct op past the result cut.

We can confirm the index is current, so this is not staleness: keywords we published recently do work on direct probes — "ranked by commits" surfaces `getLeaderboard`, and "in the code" ranks `explainRepo` first.

### Other cases with the same shape

- "jobs, bounties and freelance work for Stellar contributors" → `getRfps` absent, though "rfps" alone ranks it first.
- "how does the Blend lending pool calculate interest" → `explainRepo` absent, though "in the code" ranks it first.

### Why we're reporting rather than patching

We've been closing routing misses by adding vocabulary to our cards, and this class does not respond to that: there is no keyword that outweighs another op's id on that id's own noun. If the intent is that a well-described op should be reachable by a natural question, this seems worth a look at the scorer — perhaps capping id weight, or guaranteeing that an op matching a high proportion of query terms survives the result cut.

Happy to run any probe you'd like against the live endpoint and report what comes back.

ID: WORLD-OW-TERRAIN-EDIT-001

Status: **PLANNED — BIOME-1 / WORLD-OW TERRAIN-MUTATION FOUNDATION / IMPLEMENTATION WIP=0**
Priority: P1 future Biome-1 composition after accepted usable Overworld terrain/runtime foundations and normal #281/#33 eligibility
Category: WORLD-OW / Terrain / World Mutation / Persistence / Collision / Building Composition
Architecture: `docs/WORLD_ARCHITECTURE.md` §9 + `docs/PERSISTENCE_AND_VERSIONING.md` §§3–4, 9, 18, 23
World roadmap: #405 Phase 2 WORLD-OW foundation
Biome-1 product/environment: #470/#498/#499
Stable-world collision/currentness: #512/#509
Building placement/support/runtime: #492/#494/#495/#503
Pending reward physical/collection safety: #507/#508
Inventory/resource authority: accepted canonical Inventory transaction architecture + explicit Stone resource sources
Persistence substrate: accepted `WorldDeltaStore.terrain_delta_index` / MAP delta family
Scale authority: #369
Board: #33

## Why this card exists

Locked world architecture already permits broad local Overworld terrain modification and locked persistence architecture already reserves terrain/material deltas against deterministic base geometry. Building architecture explicitly says terrain editing is a **separate durable world-delta family**, not an implicit Building side effect.

The first-Biome product direction now makes that previously abstract capability concrete:
- terrain shaping is a player world-editing action;
- ordinary terrain may be reshaped/lowered without becoming a resource-harvesting path;
- terrain raising/fill is available and consumes **Stone**;
- added material cost scales with the actual added terrain volume rather than one flat click fee;
- edited terrain becomes the same real persistent solid terrain used for traversal/collision and Building structural roots;
- modification is bounded relative to the deterministic **canonical/original terrain**, so repeated edits cannot ratchet the allowable vertical envelope indefinitely.

No current concrete card owns that gameplay/runtime/persistence transaction. #498 describes terrain composition, #512 supplies stable-world collision currentness, and #492/#494 consume terrain for Building, but none owns player terrain mutation itself.

Core invariant:
> **Player terrain shaping modifies one canonical Overworld terrain-delta layer over deterministic base terrain. Runtime mesh/collision are rebuildable representations of that durable delta; terrain removal yields no generic materials, while positive fill consumes authoritative Stone according to added volume.**

Planning only. This card changes no current M3/Phase-0 priority and claims no implementation source.

---

# 1. One terrain authority — deterministic base + durable delta

Do not create a parallel `player terrain`, Building floor mesh or ad-hoc voxel object system.

The effective terrain for an edited location is conceptually:

```text
pinned deterministic Overworld base terrain
+ canonical durable terrain delta
= current effective terrain
```

Requirements:
- untouched terrain remains regenerated from the pinned compatible Overworld generation contract;
- player edits live in the existing logical terrain-delta persistence family;
- runtime terrain mesh/collision/chunk caches consume base + delta;
- unloading/re-entry reconstructs identical effective terrain;
- Save/Continue reconstructs identical effective terrain before that local collision becomes authoritative;
- editing never rewrites generator seed/noise/stage truth.

Do not serialize terrain MeshInstances, collision RIDs, chunk Nodes or generated mesh vertices as durable authority.

---

# 2. First bounded shaping vocabulary

The first implementation needs only the shaping operations required by the accepted Biome-1 direction, conceptually:

```text
LOWER / EXCAVATE / SHAPE DOWN
RAISE / FILL / SHAPE UP
```

A later convenience `flatten` or smoothing action may be derived from the same canonical delta authority if product actually wants it; do not build

## Destination

An architecture in which **the sensory rim and the core are in communication**, and **each cell models its own piece's dynamics with a learned linear operator**, whose **cell contract assumes no particular world**, demonstrated in **two domains** running the same cells: the existing sandbox, and language learned conversationally from a small local interlocutor.

**Done when** the rim and the apex **influence each other** — rim cells moving the apex **collectively**, in the counted sense and not the summed one ([#232](https://github.com/NGL321/patchworks/issues/232) measured the summed sense empty); the apex moving **every** L1 cell and the actuator, individually; through an apex stable enough to conduct it — and the same cell contract, sheaf, and learning rules run both domains, each with a pre-registered acceptance demo and a settled pass condition.

**The operative bar is the rim-core influence predicate, written by [#242](https://github.com/NGL321/patchworks/issues/242) and replacing ADR-0021's ratio in that role.** It reads **time, not amplitude**: per cell, the paired counterfactual deviation in that cell's private features must have an e-fold decay time at least the tick length of the shortest loop through it that reaches the rim and returns — `min` over the cells of a path of `τ̂_c / |loop(c)| ≥ 1`, `max` over paths, median over trials. Stated twice. **Inbound**, a swept single-source count: every rim stratum's reaching set non-empty, the reached fraction published, no threshold on it yet and none needed while the reading is zero. **Outbound**, a **universal** over L1 predicting cells and the actuator boundary cell — sensory boundary cells excluded because the world's write voids what arrives, not because nothing arrives. Falsified by no loop closing on any path, or by a private-feature deviation bit-identical between branches. The shortfall today is **1.1x to 8.5x**, where the bar it replaces was short 1.3e9x. The **15.4x** this map published — `τ` at 0.91 against a 14-tick loop — was read on the chart's *direct* round trip, and [#274](https://github.com/NGL321/patchworks/issues/274) found that instrument omits the stalk relay; the corrected apex `τ` is 1.6 to 13.1 ticks over nine driven seeds. **The predicate is untouched and short on every seed** — only the magnitude moves, and the defendable claim is that 15.4x read the wrong operator, not that ~3.8x is the shortfall. Written by [#257](https://github.com/NGL321/patchworks/issues/257) as ADR-0026; amended by [#275](https://github.com/NGL321/patchworks/issues/275), **in review as [#280](https://github.com/NGL321/patchworks/pull/280)** and not landed until it merges.

**ADR-0021 is kept, not retired.** The per-edge bottleneck ratio stays the **sufficient** diagnostic [#230](https://github.com/NGL321/patchworks/issues/230) re-scoped it to, and it correctly located where the channel dies: a pass is conclusive, a fail is not. It is no longer what this map is read against. *reaches and returns* is not the claim either, per #230 and [#236](https://github.com/NGL321/patchworks/issues/236), because nothing has to arrive.

**This map has a defined negative.** If stage 2 establishes that learning cannot produce the retention gradient — [#143](https://github.com/NGL321/patchworks/issues/143)'s registered claim — that redirects this map rather than deadlocking it. **The claim is back to unchecked ([#276](https://github.com/NGL321/patchworks/issues/276)).** It was read as supported by `05:253`'s flat `τ`; but no run has ever carried a **placed** gradient, so nothing has yet tested what learning does to one.

**Recharted 2026-08-29.** This map previously gated everything on a Koopman prototype ([#126](https://github.com/NGL321/patchworks/issues/126)). # Misyra Development Ledger

This issue tracks the active implementation ticket and review state for Misyra. Development is performed as a single-agent, specification-driven workflow. GitHub history, the approved specifications, ticket acceptance criteria, tests, PR diffs, and verification evidence are authoritative.

## Authoritative sources

- `docs/specifications/product-specification.md`
- `docs/specifications/technical-specification.md`
- `docs/specifications/implementation-tickets.md`

The product specification is authoritative for user-facing behavior. The technical specification is authoritative for implementation architecture and engineering constraints. The implementation-ticket document defines dependency order, ticket scope, acceptance criteria, TDD evidence, and review gates.

## Development workflow

1. Read the exact active ticket and relevant product/technical specification sections from current `main` before modifying code.
2. Verify the required `main` base SHA and dependencies.
3. Work on exactly one ticket branch and one implementation PR at a time.
4. Use strict **RED → GREEN → REFACTOR → verification** for behavior/configuration changes.
5. Do not implement later-ticket scope.
6. Run focused and all affected format, lint, typecheck, test, build, audit, privacy, localization, infrastructure, and integration checks required by the ticket/specifications.
7. Review the actual PR diff and resolve every Important or Critical finding before merge.
8. Merge only through a PR after exact-head verification and review.
9. Record completion, then advance only to the next dependency-ready ticket.
10. Never deploy, activate production resources, introduce production credentials, mutate external providers, perform store submission, or make another gated external change without explicit user approval.
11. Preserve the approved specification documents and unrelated/user work.
12. Branch `deprecated` is reference-only.

## Repository protection

During the restart, `main` should use pull-request, branch-deletion, and non-fast-forward/force-push protections. Do not require legacy CI status contexts before **MTS-007 — Establish CI quality gates** creates stable checks.

**Temporary recovery note:** the `Protect main` ruleset exists but enforcement is disabled by explicit user authorization while autonomous recovery continues. Development still uses feature branch → PR → exact-head review → non-destructive merge. Restore enforcement after the temporary recovery window.

## Ticket states

- `READY` — dependency-ready; no implementation branch/PR active.
- `IMPLEMENTING` — implementation in progress.
- `REVIEWING` — implementation is under specification/diff review and correction.
- `MERGE_READY` — review clean and merge prerequisites satisfied.
- `BLOCKED` — cannot safely continue without an unavailable dependency or explicit decision.

**Bench-found 2026-07-27 (LS850 SN12062, LVP `0c05a97b` on `fix/small-batch-2026-07`; bundle `Firmware/build/SN12062-2026-07-27-113207/`).**

## Symptom

Two protocol runs aborted with the popup **"Camera Failure: Camera failed 3 consecutive captures. Aborting protocol."** (11:30:05 and 11:31:15). Each abort was preceded by capture rejections of the form:

```
get_image: frame chunk for exposure never matched the requested target within 1.0s (chunk=26373.0, target=100000.0) ... Capture rejected.
[PROTOCOL] Capture failed for step N ... scan N -- camera inactive or frame drain failed (failure n/3)
```

## Root chain (from the logs)

1. Operator enabled per-layer auto-gain at 11:29:39-53; the camera driver set `GainAuto=Continuous` + `ExposureAuto=Continuous` (camera.log 11:29:53.268).
2. The protocol run started at 11:29:59 and set a fixed exposure (`ExposureTime.SetValue(100000us)`, camera.log 11:30:00.822) -- but **no `auto_gain(state=False)` appears anywhere between the enable and the abort**. The camera's auto modes stayed active.
3. The capture gate waits for a frame whose chunk exposure matches the requested 100 ms. With AE still hunting, chunks came back at 26.4 ms, 55.2 ms, and pegged at 200 ms (the `ae_max_exp_ms` cap; `save_camera_state ... exp=200.0` at api.log 11:29:59.064 confirms AE had driven exposure to the cap pre-run). The gate can never match -> 3 rejections -> abort. A second run with `auto_gain=True` layers (api.log 11:30:49.634) passed one scan by luck, then aborted.

## Structural question (needs a design decision before a fix)

For a layer with auto-gain enabled, what should protocol capture do?
- (a) force auto modes OFF at protocol start and capture at stored gain/exposure;
- (b) leave AE/AG running and exempt those layers from the exposure-match gate (the gate's premise -- "frame must carry the requested exposure" -- is undefined under AE);
- (c) run a bounded converge-then-lock at scan start (converge AG, freeze values, then gate normally).

Interacts with the frame-validity exposure-gate machinery and the auto-gain settle work; a fix should not be attempted as a one-line patch to the gate.

Status: analyzed from bench logs; fix not started; not verified on hardware.
title: Auto-gain arms with a stale exposure chunk target: every frame is rejected and the protocol aborts

Single unattended controller for ZEL research-to-readiness progression. Immutable GitHub workflow artifacts are SSOT. No stage may advance without an explicit deterministic PASS receipt.

## Global locks
- Maximum one heavy VPS replay at a time.
- No duplicate strategy+axis+data-SHA replay.

- `selection_authority=false`, `promotion_authority=false`, `execution_authority=NONE`, `order_authority=BLOCKED` until the applicable later gate explicitly passes.

- [x] G1 Merge staged PR #564 into PR #560 head; accept EMA artifact
- [x] G2 Merge staged PR #565 into PR #562 head; accept Scalp artifact

Every candidate must have exact source-owner and baseline trade/economic-digest parity; W1-only selection frozen through W2/W3; complete fee/slippage/funding lineage; errors=0; duplicate=0; censored-open=0; unknown-exit=0 where applicable; no future MFE/MAE leakage; no protected mutation. Implementation/infrastructure defects: read-only diagnosis → one root cause → minimum patch → verify → at most two retries. Secret/permission/quota/external-service blockers or the same cause failing twice force HOLD and user-authority request.

The controller must maintain one latest-state comment on this issue containing: stage, active PR/run/job, head SHA, artifact SHA, PASS/FAIL/HOLD, gate evidence, retry count, current blocker, next permitted action, and confirmation that Live/order authority is blocked. ## Purpose

This issue is the authoritative coordination root for the Veritas multi-agent roadmap.

The goal is to make the entire remaining program independently pick-up-able by agents without overlapping ownership, while keeping completed/active work visible and preserving dependency order.

## Work-state protocol

Every executable roadmap issue must contain a machine-readable **Work Contract** with:

- Work ID
- state: `BLOCKED | READY | CLAIMED | REVIEW | DONE | SUPERSEDED`
- dependencies
- branch name
- positive path ownership
- negative path ownership
- acceptance criteria
- falsifiers
- evidence/qualification boundary
- claim holder / claim timestamp / heartbeat
- linked PR

Until the automated claim workflow lands, agents claim work by posting exactly:

`/claim <agent-id> <branch>`

and must immediately check that no earlier un-released claim exists on the issue before editing. They announce handoff with:

`/handoff <agent-id> <pr-number>`

and completion with:

`/done <agent-id> <pr-number>`

A claim is not an authorization to merge, release, run sealed/manual workflows, spend money, expose private data, or weaken qualification gates.

## Concurrency rule

Two active work items may run in parallel only when:

1. neither depends on the other;
2. their positive ownership paths are disjoint;
3. neither item edits the other's negative ownership paths;
4. no shared/root integration path is claimed by both;
5. provider/schema lanes merge before dependent consumer lanes;
6. dependent branches sync/rebase onto merged `main` and rerun exact-head gates.

Shared/root integration work is serialized through explicit convergence tickets.

## Current active implementation

- #134 — canonical structured investigation corpus compiler
- #147 — Gold-10 receipt acquisition
- #149 — Machine Experience / EXP-001 foundation
- #65 — Frontier Qualification remains draft/manual-boundary work
- #118 — legacy public-investigation stack; do not merge as-is; migration/supersession work only

## Program centers

- #130 — High-Stakes Investigation / Gold flagship
- #146 — Machine Experience / Learning Readiness
- #148 — Learning Efficiency
- #63 — Frontier Qualification

## Roadmap structure

Child executable tickets are being created and linked from this issue in dependency order. This root issue should remain open until the roadmap registry has been fully decomposed and the claim automation is operational.

## Coordination invariants

- no work may be silently claimed only in chat;
- every active agent must leave a visible claim on the issue before editing;
- every PR must link its Work ID/issue;
- no agent may opportunistically edit another claimed lane;
- stale claims must be explicitly released/reassigned rather than ignored;
- `UNKNOWN` evidence never becomes PASS because another lane completed;
- completed work is closed only after its integration/evidence boundary is satisfied, not merely because code exists.

## Next coordination implementation

A repository-native issue-comment workflow will automate `/claim`, `/release`, `/handoff`, `/blocked`, and `/done` state transitions and create/use status labels so agents can query ready vs claimed work directly.

**Interpretation.**

`LOCAL-003` applies because #41 creates the dedicated Windows group used for transport/start eligibility. That membership must **never** become enrollment, reactivation, Owner-establishment, or Manager authorization authority.

`LOCAL-004` applies at the activation boundary even though #41 implements no local IPC or TLS. #41 must preserve the distinction: an **absent or refused endpoint** may lead later client code to invoke `IHostActivation`; an **endpoint that exists but fails Host authentication is a security failure** and must never be treated as "still starting". #41 does not implement that connection state machine — #42 does.

## Authorized scope

### Host-side Windows platform

**1. `Platform.Contracts`** — bounded contracts for `IHostServiceLifecycle`, `IBootStartPlatform`, and Windows machine-wide Host-data-root discovery through the existing platform abstraction model. Exact internal type naming is an allowed decision.

**2. Windows service runtime** — `System.ServiceProcess.ServiceController` **8.0.1** in `Platform.Windows`, authorized for two purposes: `ServiceBase` for the actual SCM process lifetime, and `ServiceController` where useful for privileged lifecycle operations. **No `Microsoft.Extensions.Hosting` or `Microsoft.Extensions.Hosting.WindowsServices`.**

Wrapper/class organization is an allowed decision.

## Summary

Harden the OAuth authorization flow so dynamically registered clients always require explicit consent and receive standards-compliant authorization and token errors. This is a regression follow-up to #97: the provider callback currently issues a code directly instead of returning the authenticated user to the approval UI.

## Findings

- **high** — Dynamically registered clients can receive authorization codes without explicit user consent (`fnd_sig-feat-route-f70e828f34-e3b204_8841e98421`).
- **medium** — Authorization denial does not return `error=access_denied` and the original `state` to the client (`fnd_sig-feat-route-47fdf648bb-f82e29_f2e49e7fa5`).
- **medium** — Authorization errors remain local JSON responses after a safe redirect URI is established (`fnd_sig-feat-route-f70e828f34-82bfdd_cbe5c33a25`).
- **medium** — Requested scopes are issued without validation against the supported read/write scopes (`fnd_sig-feat-route-38c6bdc367-bf0766_8cdaabfbeb`).
- **medium** — Token endpoint errors are serialized under FastAPI's non-standard `detail` envelope (`fnd_sig-feat-route-160a31e8d6-23b0b1_5e93157586`).
- **low** — S256 PKCE challenges are accepted without validating the required 43-character unpadded base64url format (`fnd_sig-feat-route-f70e828f34-336b39_7fe54ac551`).

## Reproduction steps

1. Register a dynamic loopback client and initiate `/authorize` with PKCE and `state`.
2. Complete provider login and observe that the provider callback can return a code without POSTing the CSRF-protected approval form.
3. On separate requests, deny authorization, request an unknown scope, provide a malformed S256 challenge, or submit an otherwise redirectable invalid authorization request.
4. POST an invalid grant to `/token` and inspect the JSON response.

## Expected behavior

The authenticated user must explicitly approve or deny the pending client request. Safe authorization errors and denial must return to the validated client URI with the original state. Unsupported scopes and malformed PKCE challenges must be rejected before code issuance, and token errors must use the OAuth top-level error shape with no-store headers.

## Actual behavior

The provider callback bypasses consent; denial redirects to `/connect`; redirectable authorization errors are emitted locally; arbitrary scopes and malformed challenges survive authorization; and token errors are wrapped as `{"detail":{"error":...}}`.

## Impact

A public dynamic client can obtain a grant without the intended user decision, while protocol mismatches cause legitimate OAuth clients to hang or misinterpret failures. Unvalidated scopes create a future privilege-escalation hazard if another component recognizes an injected scope.

## Proposed Direction

- Preserve the pending request after provider login and route back to the consent UI; issue codes only through the approval endpoint.
- Revalidate and consume pending state on denial, returning `access_denied` and `state` only to an already validated redirect URI.
- Establish client and redirect validity before converting later authorization failures to OAuth redirect errors.
- Validate requested scopes against the supported allowlist and validate S256 challenge syntax in initial and pending request paths.
- Emit top-level OAuth JSON errors from token-style endpoints, including appropriate cache headers.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Provider-login and existing-session paths both require CSRF-protected explicit approval before code issuance.
- Denial returns `error=access_denied` and unchanged `state` to the validated redirect URI; malformed pending data never causes an external redirect.
- Invalid response type, PKCE, and scope errors follow OAuth redirect/error semantics once the redirect target is trusted.
- Unknown or mixed unsupported scopes never reach a code or token record.
- `/token` failures contain a top-level `error`, no `detail`, and no-store cache headers.

# Independent Review Queue

This issue is the **single review entrypoint** for the Second Brain repository.

Human shorthand command:

> `验算第二大脑`

The reviewer must NOT guess from “latest open PR”. This repository may have historical/frozen Draft PRs and multiple legitimate parallel engineering lines.

## Queue model: append-only exact-head tickets

Engineering posts `REVIEW_REQUEST/v1` only after a bounded slice reaches its independent-review stop gate. Ticket identity is `(pr, exact_head)`.

Reviewer appends `REVIEW_RESULT/v1` for that exact ticket:

```yaml
schema: REVIEW_RESULT/v1
project: SECOND_BRAIN
pr: <number>
reviewed_head: <sha>
verdict: ACCEPT | CHANGES_REQUIRED | BLOCKED
review_evidence_ref: <PR review/comment URL or id>
review_channel: GITHUB_APPROVE | EXACT_HEAD_COMMENT_ATTESTATION
reviewer_agent_id: GPT_INDEPENDENT_REVIEWER
independence_attestation: NO_PRODUCTION_CODE_OR_REMEDIATION_ON_REVIEWED_HEAD
```

A request is pending iff no later result exists for the exact same `(pr, exact_head)`. Remediation creates a new exact head and therefore a new request.

## Same-account GitHub APPROVE limitation

All ChatGPT engineering/reviewer windows currently operate through the same linked GitHub account. GitHub may reject a formal APPROVE with `Review Can not approve your own pull request`.

This platform limitation MUST NOT be bypassed or misrepresented.

When formal APPROVE is unavailable for this reason, the canonical independent-review evidence for our workflow is:

1. an exact-head PR review **COMMENT** containing the independent architecture/adversarial review;
2. a matching append-only `REVIEW_RESULT/v1` here with `verdict: ACCEPT` or `CHANGES_REQUIRED`;
3. exact `reviewed_head` equality with the current PR head at review completion;
4. reviewer role separation: the reviewing ChatGPT window did not implement or remediate the reviewed head;
5. fresh CI/current-main verification where required by the task.

`EXACT_HEAD_COMMENT_ATTESTATION + REVIEW_RESULT/v1` is therefore sufficient **workflow acceptance evidence** when same-account APPROVE is mechanically unavailable. It is not represented as GitHub platform approval.

If a genuinely separate GitHub reviewer identity is available later, `GITHUB_APPROVE` may be used as stronger platform evidence, but it is not required for the current multi-window workflow.

## Reviewer procedure for `验算第二大脑`

1. Read this issue and all comments.
2. Compute pending exact-head tickets only.
3. Fresh verify PR head and current `main`; stale/moved heads fail closed.
4. Process serially by priority then request time.
5. Read protocol_ref, source Issue, PR body/diff/tests/CI/prior review threads.
6. Perform independent architecture/adversarial validation. CI green is evidence, not acceptance authority.

## 目的

Crownless を、スケジュール実行するAIエージェントが自分で次の遊びを考え、Issue化し、実装まで進める「自律プロダクト開発」のPOCとして記録する。

将来の出版・振り返りで、単なるGit履歴では分からない **AIが何を考え、なぜそれを選び、人間がどこで介入したか** を一次資料として残す。

このIssueは実装タスクではなく、実験ログの正本として扱う。原則closeせず、各自律開発サイクルをコメントで追記する。

## 各サイクルで残す内容

### 1. Cycle
- 実行日時（Asia/Tokyo）
- 起動種別: scheduled / human-triggered
- 対象main SHA（取得できる場合）

### 2. AI proposal
- 直近3〜5サイクルで新しい遊びが増えたか
- 新機能候補3案
- 各候補の4軸スコア
  - プレイヤーが気づく変化
  - 新しい判断
  - リプレイ性
  - Canonとの整合

### 3. Decision
- 今回選んだIssue / 新規アイデア
- なぜそれを選んだか
- 他候補を選ばなかった主な理由
- bug-fix / maintenance / innovation の区分

### 4. Execution
- 新規Issue / 既存Issue
- 実装した縦切り
- PR / commit
- test / CI
- merge / close結果

### 5. Human intervention
前回サイクル以降、人間による方向修正がGitHub上または実行コンテキストから確認できる場合に記録する。

例:
- 新しいIssueを人間が追加した
- AI案を却下・修正した
- 優先順位を変更した
- 実装済み機能の作り直しを指示した
- 直接エージェントへ割り込んだ

介入が確認できなければ `なし / 確認できず` とし、推測で人間介入を作らない。

### 6. Outcome / observation
- プレイヤーから見て何が変わったか
- 新しい遊び・判断が増えたか
- AIの判断で気になった点
- 次回観察したいこと

## 記録原則

- 事実とAIの評価を分ける
- 後から書き換えず、原則コメントを追加して時系列を保つ
- Issue/PR/commitへリンクできる情報を残す
- 長い実装ログやCI全文は複製せず、意思決定に必要な要約だけを残す
- 人間介入は確認できたものだけを記録し、推測しない
- 成功だけでなく、`no_action`、失敗、誤った提案、revert、方向修正も残す

## このPOCで検証したい問い

> AIは、与えられたIssueを消化するだけでなく、自分で「次に何を作るべきか」を考え、ゲームを継続的に面白くできるか。

> 人間は常時開発ループを回さず、必要なときだけIssue追加や直接指示で介入する運用へ移れるか。

Related: #228
title: POC: AI自律開発の意思決定・人間介入ログ

Locked world architecture already permits broad local Overworld terrain modification and locked persistence architecture already reserves terrain/material deltas against deterministic base geometry. Building architecture explicitly says terrain editing is a **separate durable world-delta family**, not an implicit Building side effect.

The first-Biome product direction now makes that previously abstract capability concrete:
- terrain shaping is a player world-editing action;
- ordinary terrain may be reshaped/lowered without becoming a resource-harvesting path;
- terrain raising/fill is available and consumes **Stone**;
- added material cost scales with the actual added terrain volume rather than one flat click fee;
- edited terrain becomes the same real persistent solid terrain used for traversal/collision and Building structural roots;

No current concrete card owns that gameplay/runtime/persistence transaction. #498 describes terrain composition, #512 supplies stable-world collision currentness, and #492/#494 consume terrain for Building, but none owns player terrain mutation itself.

Core invariant:
> **Player terrain shaping modifies one canonical Overworld terrain-delta layer over deterministic base terrain. Runtime mesh/collision are rebuildable representations of that durable delta; terrain removal yields no generic materials, while positive fill consumes authoritative Stone according to added volume.**

Planning only. This card changes no current M3/Phase-0 priority and claims no implementation source.

```text
+ canonical durable terrain delta
= current effective terrain
```

Requirements:
- untouched terrain remains regenerated from the pinned compatible Overworld generation contract;
- player edits live in the existing logical terrain-delta persistence family;
- runtime terrain mesh/collision/chunk caches consume base + delta;
- unloading/re-entry reconstructs identical effective terrain;
- Save/Continue reconstructs identical effective terrain before that local collision becomes authoritative;
- editing never rewrites generator seed/noise/stage truth.

Do not serialize terrain MeshInstances, collision RIDs, chunk Nodes or generated mesh vertices as durable authority.

Implement the First Playable cargo-loss rule without deleting equipment or spawning dozens of loose item Nodes:

Multiple Death Caches may coexist. A later death does not delete the earlier cache.

Death must first build one detached authoritative disposition plan from current canonical ownership.

Classify each owned item/copy exactly once into:
- retained equipped ownership;
- retained essential Core Tool ownership according to accepted product definition;
- cache cargo.

Do not infer retention merely from Item family name in UI or from hotbar reference. Canonical Equipment/Core-Tool semantics determine it.

Examples:
- actually equipped Sword -> retained;
- spare Sword in Inventory -> cargo;
- equipped armor pieces -> retained;
- one canonical essential Pickaxe/Hoe/Build Tool as defined by the current Core-Tool policy -> retained;
- spare copies remain ordinary cargo unless explicitly part of the Core-Tool ownership model.

Hotbar is quick access, not a second ownership container.

---

# 2. Failure-atomic death transaction

Cargo transfer is one authoritative operation:
1. freeze exact current Player ownership snapshot/revision for the death operation;
2. classify retained vs cache cargo;
3. choose/validate canonical cache world identity and recoverable location from the actual death context;
4. construct detached cache container state;
5. atomically commit Player Inventory removal + durable cache creation;
6. only then allow the death lifecycle to proceed to recovery/respawn commit.

If cache creation cannot be committed durably, do not silently delete cargo.

A repeated/stale death completion callback cannot create a second cache from the same owned items.

---

# 3. Cache identity/location

Each cache needs stable semantic identity independent from runtime presentation, including:
- cache occurrence/operation identity;
- owner player identity;
- exact world/domain/root identity;
- recoverable world location/candidate;
- canonical container contents.

Runtime marker/model/collider identity is not durable truth.

The cache remains in the domain where death actually occurred even if the player respawns elsewhere.

If exact death coordinates are inside now-invalid/destructible geometry, use a deterministic nearby safe/recoverable placement policy. Do not teleport the cache to the Bed/World Spawn merely for convenience.

---

# 4. Multiple caches

If a player dies again before recovering Cache A:
- Cache A remains canonical;
- second eligible cargo set creates Cache B;

## Purpose

This issue is the durable coordination, queue, lease, recovery and handoff point for Dungeon Veil autonomous work. GitHub is the source of truth. Chat reports are informational only. Replit is forbidden.

## Active operating model: exactly two regular workers

Dungeon Veil uses exactly two regular ChatGPT automation roles in `Europe/Berlin`. Their actual enabled schedules are external automation state and must be read live; do not hard-code clock times here or infer them from historical comments.

1. **Master implementer** (`worker: primary`)

   - implements, tests, commits, pushes and maintains its PR;
   - creates a risk-based exact-head test plan and inspects the selected evidence;
   - may carry a fully accepted exact head through Ready, merge and publication.
2. **Master verifier** (`worker: verifier`)
   - independently verifies the risk classification, test-plan mapping, exact-head gates, reviews, threads and evidence;
   - expands an understated plan and may safely fix focused defects when no primary scope overlaps;
   - performs final acceptance, Expected-Head merge without auto-merge, retains branches and verifies deployment.

The actual enabled automation configuration is authoritative for execution times. If repository text and live automation state disagree only about schedule, correct the stale documentation; do not change worker scope or create an extra regular worker just to match an old clock time.

There are no active scheduled `secondary` or `visual` workers. Old comments using those worker names are historical records only and do not authorize new work. Do not create additional regular workers unless the user explicitly changes this operating model after concrete evidence that two workers are insufficient.

`worker: background` is permitted only for an explicitly separate, short-lived coordination or migration task. It is never a third scheduled product worker.

## Immutable project rules

- repository: `ys2mm422yb-max/DungeonVeil`
- only target, test and publication branch: `fix/mobile-telegraphs-room-21-50-balance`
- only public test URL: `https://ys2mm422yb-max.github.io/DungeonVeil/`

- do not weaken assertions, coverage, thresholds, acceptance criteria or timeouts
- evidence follows Issue #366 budgets and SHA-256 deduplication
- no temporary GitHub Actions workflows as patch transport

A known defect, rejecting user report, unresolved review requirement, unreviewed visual issue or unmet acceptance criterion blocks Ready and merge.

## Mandatory work order and state machines

Finish existing priority work before opening unnecessary new PRs. Current order is maintained in the newest handoffs below.

Primary state machine:
`IMPLEMENTIEREN -> TESTPLAN -> EXAKT-HEAD-TESTS -> EVIDENCE -> READY -> READY-GATES -> MERGE -> DEPLOY -> DONE`

Verifier state machine:
`VERIFY -> TESTPLAN-REVIEW -> EVIDENCE -> READY-GATES -> MERGE -> DEPLOY -> DONE`

A worker may not report the same exact head, state and blocker for three consecutive runs without a new concrete action. `waiting_external` is not a run-ending condition when independent work is available.

At the start of every pass read this issue and its newest comments, `AGENTS.md`, `docs/ADAPTIVE_TEST_POLICY.md`, roadmap #323, open issues, PRs, reviews, exact-head Actions, artifacts, deployments and current user feedback.

Gameplay feedback/guidance: #476/#477/#481/#482/#486
Persistence/startup: accepted SAVE/GameFlow authorities + whichever domain/startup contracts are accepted when this gate becomes executable
Scale/performance: #369
Roadmap/board: #405/#33

## Why this card exists

The first-Biome planning graph now has bounded owners for the individual systems and #496 specifically proves the **fresh-run bootstrap is acyclic/reachable**.

That is necessary but not sufficient for the product goal:

> **Biome 1 should be a genuinely enjoyable, self-contained first playable space that supports extended exploration, hunting, combat, recovery and expressive wood Building without requiring cave/Underworld progression.**

A build can pass every child card independently and still fail as a game because the systems interact badly over a real session:
- the opening works but ordinary exploration becomes continuous combat;
- Wood economy supports one Workbench but makes actual Building grindy;
- 16 Inventory slots fit a fixture but become hostile after hunting + building + weapon experimentation;
- berries/Fox/Rootwretches permanently deplete so quickly that the local world feels dead after 30 minutes;
- Save/Continue reconstructs each subsystem in isolation but loses a cross-system relationship;
- dense woodland makes combat unreadable or runtime expensive;
- Building works technically but correction/deconstruction is punitive;
- guidance becomes necessary to discover a hidden prerequisite order;
- an accidental cave/Underworld/pickaxe dependency remains in an otherwise surface-only feature.

This card is the **integrated product/QA exit gate** for the first Overworld biome.

It does not implement the child systems, own balance data, or become one mega-source task.

Core invariant:
> **Acceptance proves the composition players actually experience, not merely that every subsystem has a passing unit/integration test.**

---

# 1. Two-layer acceptance model

Use both:

### A. Deterministic automated/composition scenarios
Prove exact cross-system invariants repeatably across a representative deterministic root set.

### B. Human extended-session acceptance
Prove the biome is readable, pleasant and worth continuing to play when the player is not following a scripted test path.

Neither substitutes for the other.

Automated checks cannot prove combat/building feel.
Human play cannot replace deterministic persistence/economy correctness.

---

# 2. Bootstrap scenario — consume #496, do not duplicate it

The first gate begins with a true NEW_GAME state and consumes #496's accepted matrix.

Reference path only, not a quest order:

```text
NEW GAME
-> orient in valid #498 soft-start environment
-> gather enough loose Wood + Loose Stone
-> hand-craft Axe
-> harvest a tree efficiently
-> place a few wood structural pieces
-> build Basic Workbench
-> craft one real Workbench-required item

-> survive/defeat the intended first ordinary hostile encounter
```

Required:
- no test-only item grants after startup;
- no direct service mutation to skip real interactions;
- no tutorial flag required;
- player may reorder optional operations where gameplay permits.

#496 remains the detailed bootstrap authority. Failure here blocks this gate but is repaired through the owning child card.

## Goal

Use a citizen's declared `profession` and `vocation` as soft orientation signals when several useful next actions exist, without restricting what the citizen may choose or turning identity text into authorization.

## Context

Measured on 2026-09-02 during Aurora's first autonomous run. Aurora declared `profession: Software Producer`, then generic Academy guidance led her directly into the browser rung and a local Chromium installation. That action was legitimate autonomous behavior; the product gap is that the Colony had stronger profession context available but did not use it to orient the menu of next steps.

`profession` and `vocation` are free-text self-declarations. They must remain descriptive, unverified, and non-gating.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] When wakeup or Academy can offer multiple valid next actions, its structured and rendered guidance may explain which option best matches the citizen's declared profession or vocation.
- [ ] The signal is advisory only: it does not hide, reject, rank for rewards, auto-claim, or authorize tasks.
- [ ] Null, blank, novel, or ambiguous profession text falls back to current behavior without error.
- [ ] The response distinguishes Colony facts from an inferred profession match.
- [ ] Updating `profession` does not alter skills, standing, eligibility, permissions, or active work.
- [ ] The orientation adds no duplicate workflow state outside the existing wakeup, task, and Workplace sources of truth.

## Definition of done

- [ ] Tests cover a Software Producer, an unrelated profession, null profession, and the non-interference invariants.
- [ ] Structured response and concise MCP rendering are both tested.
- [ ] `npm run check` passes.

## Related

- Profession identity/orientation implementation and its existing free-text semantics.

## Out of scope

- Profession enums or classification as identity truth.
- Profession-specific Academy tracks.
- Restricting autonomous tool use or local software installation.
- Automatic task claiming.
title: Make profession a soft orientation signal in wakeup and Academy guidance

### Desired outcome

`phylo.learn.Environment` gains two instances beside the 1-D Potts chain: the Potts lattice, over the graphs #170 generates, and the HMM state path, over the single-position moves #176 implements. Nothing under `phylo.learn` learns what a lattice or a sequence is.

### Why it matters

`ROADMAP.md` §2.1 requires an MDP defined across all three problem classes — state, action and reward stated for each. Today `phylo.learn` carries one reference instance, a 1-D Potts chain, and the tree environment lives in `phylo.search.rl`.

The model-agnosticism of `phylo.opt.Objective` is not asserted but measured: four instances run against it unchanged, and none required a change to `phylo.opt`. `phylo.learn.Environment` makes the same claim on the strength of one instance, and an interface justified by a single model is shaped by that model. This is what would make the claim comparable.

### Submodule

`search`

### Scope and non-goals

Two environments and their move sets. No new estimator, no PPO, no critic, no curriculum, no feature engineering beyond what each environment must expose for a linear policy to score its actions.

Depends on #170 for the lattice graphs and #176 for the state-path move set.

### How it will be validated

The enumerated oracle in `phylo.learn.exact` applies to any environment with a finite action set and horizon, so it carries these two as it carries the chain: the expected return is exact by trajectory enumeration and its gradient by differentiating it, and both are checked against central finite differences. Report the realized agreement against the 1.5e-11 relative already measured for the chain, at a horizon where `|A|**horizon` is affordable.

Each environment is then checked to reach its exhaustively enumerated optimum where enumeration is affordable — 3^9 configurations for a 3-state 3x3 lattice, m^L paths for a short sequence — so "the agent found the best state" has an answer rather than an opinion.

An import-graph test asserts `phylo.learn` imports nothing from `phylo.sim`, `phylo.likelihood` or `phylo.search`, the guard `phylo.opt` already carries, so the separation cannot decay by convenience import.
title: Potts lattice and HMM environments behind phylo.learn.Environment

# JOB-13 — FoxNet Online Vehicle Auctions

**Owner:** David / Captain  
**Status:** Planning and contract integration in regular chat  
**Primary dependency:** JOB-02 Career/RLS bridge  
**Cross-job sources:** JOB-04 Wrecking Yard, JOB-09 Tow Yard/lien vehicles, personal Career vehicles, company-owned vehicles  
**UI host dependency:** JOB-01 phone/PC/IceFox platform

## Mission

Build the authoritative RedFox/FoxNet online vehicle-auction system for:

- Wrecking Yard-owned vehicles exported by JOB-04,
- clear-title tow/lien vehicles exported by JOB-09,
- personal owned Career vehicles,
- company-owned vehicles,
- generated auction stock that becomes real inventory only after a completed purchase,
- multi-lot timed bidding, settlement, shipping, delivery and recent auction history.

This is an online-only auction website. It has no physical auction lane, auction-yard intake, preview trip, pickup location or required transport-to-auction job.

## Locked owner decisions

- Multiple vehicle lots may be active at the same time.
- Lot closing times should normally be staggered.
- Players may watch and bid on several vehicles simultaneously.
- Player bids may be cancelled until that lot's timer reaches zero.
- No positive reserve prices.
- No seller approval or reserve-not-met flow.
- If nobody places a valid bid, the lot is No Sale.
- Selected No Sale vehicles may be relisted; others may be returned to their source or removed.
- Purchased vehicles are shipped and enter an In Transit state before garage delivery.
- No physical vehicle viewing is required.
- Fox Facts, condition, damaged parts, missing parts, mileage and start/run/drive status influence value and bidder interest.
- The website retains one completed auction's public results until the next auction completes.
- Membership/subscription tiers may control bidding access, vehicle-value limits, buying power and fee/shipping discounts.

## Shared Sell-page rule

Only vehicles legally owned by the player, a company, JOB-04 or JOB-09 may appear as disposition candidates.

Supported actions may include:

```text
Direct Sell
Send to Auction
Relist
Strip for Parts
Scrap
Return to Yard
```

Dealership, BeamBook and Wrecking Yard browse listings are not owned vehicles merely because they are visible for sale. They must first be purchased or legally claimed.

## Required read-first files

```text
PROJECT_MANIFESTS/JOB_HANDOFFS/JOB-09_TO_JOB-13_COPART_AUCTION_HANDOFF_2026-07-29.md
PROJECT_MANIFESTS/JOB_HANDOFFS/JOB-04_TO_JOB-13_WRECKING_YARD_ONLINE_AUCTION_AND_SHARED_SELL_INVENTORY_HANDOFF_2026-07-29.md
PROJECT_MANIFESTS/INTERFACES/redfox_auction_bridge_v1.schema.json
PROJECT_MANIFESTS/INTERFACES/examples/redfoxAuctionBridge_JOB13_example.lua
PROJECT_MANIFESTS/INTERFACES/examples/copart_weui_test_harness_example.lua
PROJECT_MANIFESTS/INTERFACES/examples/auction_web_bridge_example.js
```

## Ownership boundaries

- JOB-13 must not directly edit JOB-09's `settings/redfox/tow_recovery_dispatch_yard.json`.
- JOB-13 must not directly edit JOB-04's authoritative Wrecking Yard/source records.
- JOB-13 must not directly replace stock Career/RLS files.
- Money, ownership, inventory IDs and garage placement remain authoritative through JOB-02/Career/RLS.
- JOB-04 remains authoritative for its owned Wrecking Yard inventory and disposition eligibility.
- JOB-09 remains authoritative for custody, lien eligibility, title acquisition and safe removal of its claimed vehicles during settlement.
- JOB-01 remains authoritative for phone/PC/IceFox app hosting and routing.

## Required source contract

For owned/exported vehicles, use exact Career/RLS inventory IDs and persistent source record IDs. Do not generate synthetic native inventory or shop IDs.

Each export should preserve:

- source type and source record ID,
- exact inventory ID where one exists,
- model and configuration,
- mileage,
- real condition data,
- damaged and missing parts,
- ownership/claim status,
- estimated value,
- suggested ope

## Destination

A locked set of decisions — recorded here — that fully specify a **Dutch-learning system living in this public repo and site**: the skill(s) that run sessions, the form of the content they produce, the sources and curriculum behind them, the learner profile that personalises them, and where it all surfaces on the site. The map ends when `/to-spec` can be run against it to produce a build spec. **Planning only — this map decides, it does not build.**

## Notes

**Domain**: language learning as a repo-native, agent-driven practice inside an Astro personal site (`atilileri.github.io`).

**Locked at charting time** (from the destination grilling — not re-openable without redrawing the map):

- **Goal**: the Dutch citizenship / inburgering exam, with sessions kept deliberately **a little above** exam level so the pass is comfortable. Not general fluency for its own sake. **Resolved by #77**: the target is **B1** (Staatsexamen NT2 Programma I), and "a little above" means **B2 (Programma II)** — same four skills, one rung up.
- **Publicness**: **everything is public.** Lessons, vocabulary, the learner profile, progress — all committed and published. Learning in public. Design every artifact knowing a stranger will read it.
- **Languages**: content is **Turkish-first**. The user's decision, made 2026-08-17 after reading #78: *"I want to study in Turkish."* Generated teaching output is Turkish, **except word hints and resemblances**, which use English where English is the better bridge. Dutch is the subject, not a content language.
- **The bridge is taught in both languages.** #78 recommended English-only mediation on the evidence that a Turkish/English bilingual recruits the English system for a Germanic L3. The user has overridden the *exclusivity*, not the finding: teach the bridge in **English and Turkish**, and where an intuition will silently mislead from **either** language, flag it for **both**. English carries the Germanic cognate work; Turkish carries the study experience.
- **Deadline**: none set. Invest in the system; there is runway.
- **Invocation shape** (the north star for the skill work): `/<dutch-skill> i want to do a lesson about last superbowl` → the agent teaches **whatever is next in the plan**, dressed in the **user-supplied context**. Topic is a *theme*, never a curriculum override.
- **Mobile answering** is a nice-to-have: research it, decide it, but it must not block the core.

**Skills every session should consult**: `/grilling` and `/domain-modeling` on every ticket. ## Summary

Make the Dynamo frontend, router, and sidecars runtime-optional: the scheduling core (selection, booking, KV indexing, disaggregated coordination) becomes a runtime-free library that the frontend embeds, the EPP embeds, and a standalone service exposes; request dispatch gains a direct native-gRPC transport beside the runtime request plane; worker registration and liveness move to an HTTP catalog with leases fed by sidecar agents, a Kubernetes pod feeder, or a static file; and etcd/NATS become Cargo features rather than unconditional dependencies. End state: one selection implementation serves aggregated, disaggregated, and encoder pools in every host, and a frontend plus prefill/decode workers can run on a bare VM or a Kubernetes pod with zero etcd or NATS processes. The frontend's runtime-backed path stays available where discovery, request plane, and event plane are wanted.

## Motivation

- Two selection implementations drifted: the frontend's runtime-bound `KvScheduler` and the standalone `SelectionService` used by the EPP. Every routing improvement had to land twice, and the EPP path lagged on shared-cache hits, LoRA narrowing, session context, router hints, and busy evaluation.
- Disaggregated routing was prefill-first with implicit compensation: a prefill booking that failed after decode was committed had no defined recovery, and the EPP had an open `TODO(epp-atomic-admission)`.
- Deployments needed etcd and NATS even when neither was used for anything but discovery and a request hop; small deployments and third-party gateways could not adopt the router without adopting the runtime.
- Sidecar-backed workers paid a request-plane hop on every request although the engine already exposed a native gRPC service.
- Test gaps: the runtime scheduler's error mapping for a dropped direct-dispatch stream was not migratable, the embedded partition did not feed overload detection, and decode-first coordination was silently inert. These were found and fixed while proving the exit gates below.

## Proposal

Five contracts, each with exactly one definition consumed by frontend, EPP, and sidecar. They are documented in-repo at `docs/fern/pages/developer-guide/knowledge-base/concepts/system-architecture/runtime-optional-frontend.md` and `docs/fern/pages/developer-guide/knowledge-base/modular-components/router/standalone-selection.md`.

1. **Selection seam.** Selection plus booking sit below; transport, retry, and migration sit above. Booking ownership across dispatch failure, release on redispatch, and prefill-complete via the response-stream callback. `SelectionHostHooks` let a host inject the prefill load estimator, overload and availability providers, shared cache, LoRA filter, overlap-refresh source, scheduler-load sink, and replica-sync channels.
2. **Routing inputs.** The preprocessed bundle handed to selection: token ids and hashes, ISL, LoRA, structured session context, priority, routing constraints, multimodal hashes, expected output tokens, router-hint chain.
3. **Dispatch.** A second `RoutingHost` transport: direct native-gRPC to workers that advertise an endpoint. Cancellation propagation, first-token signal, and an error taxonomy in which transport loss maps to a migratable error so the retry manager moves the request.
4. **Registration and liveness.** Catalog record schema plus TTL leases and heartbeats; drain semantics; data-parallel layout; per-rank KV-event and replay endpoints; role-to-instance routing. Feeders: sidecar self-registration, a Kubernetes label-selector pod feeder, and a static workers file.
5. **Disaggregated coordination.** A decode-anchored linked-booking state machine: advisory decode preview, optional prefill busy read, conditional-disagg policy, decode commit pinned to the previewed worker, prefill commit constrained to the decode worker's KV-transfer domain, and explicit compensation for every partial state (free decode or bypass-on-decode). Cross-pool atomicity is explicitly waived; decod
title: DEP: Runtime-optional frontend, router, and sidecars on a shared selection core

Follow-up from [#202](https://github.com/karlssberg/Motiv/issues/202), which made `MotivLimits.MaxEvaluationSize` bound one *evaluation* rather than one *fold* — on the synchronous folds only.

## What is fixed, and what is not

`EvaluationBudget` is a `[ThreadStatic]` counter that `EvaluationFold.Fold` claims at the outermost entry and every nested fold inherits, so a decorator between two operator layers now spends its caller's budget. `AsyncEvaluationFold.FoldAsync` still holds `var size = 1` in a local, so `EvaluateAsync` and `MatchesAsync` admit a decorator-layered composition that `Evaluate` and `Matches` refuse.

Held as behaviour by `DecoratorSeamTests.Should_not_yet_bound_a_decorator_layered_async_evaluation` — 50 layers of 10 operands, over a thousand nodes, evaluating under a limit of 100. Flip it to a `ThrowAsync` when this lands.

## Why the carrier is the whole problem

A thread-static is *correct* for the synchronous folds: `Evaluate` and `Matches` never leave the thread that started them, which is also why it is free — and `Matches` allocates nothing, a contract Spec 3E paid for with a per-thread frame buffer and `EvaluationBudgetTests.Should_carry_the_budget_without_allocating` now holds at 0 bytes.

It is *wrong* for the asynchronous fold. A continuation may resume on a thread whose slot holds a **suspended** evaluation's count — not a stale one, a live one. Two concurrent async evaluations interleaving on a pool thread would corrupt each other's counts in both directions: an undercount weakens the bound, an overcount refuses a composition that is within it.

## The three decisions this needs

1. **The carrier.** `AsyncLocal<T>` is the obvious answer, and its write is an `ExecutionContext` copy — affordable next to the state machine an async evaluation already allocates per operand, which is the same trade Spec 3E made when it gave the asynchronous fold a fresh frame array rather than a cached one. The value has to be a mutable box rather than an `int`, since a write per node is not affordable.

2. **What a concurrent operator's fan-out does to one counter.** `AsyncAndSpec`, `AsyncOrSpec` and `AsyncXOrSpec` take a `concurrent` flag and evaluate both operands through `Task.WhenAll`. `ExecutionContext` flows into both branches, so both would see the same box and race on it. `Interlocked.Increment` is correct and cheap here; whether the *bound* should then be checked per increment or sampled is a design question, because a fan-out can pass the limit in two branches at once.

3. **Where an `AsyncLocal` budget meets the thread-static one.** An asynchronous composition can contain a synchronous spec through `SyncSpecAsyncAdapter`, whose evaluation runs a synchronous fold. That fold reads the thread-static, finds nothing, and starts a fresh budget — so the asymmetry does not disappear when the asynchronous side is fixed; it moves. Either both folds read one carrier, or the seam is documented as another exclusion.

## Not in scope

The asynchronous fold's *depth*. `#145` measured the async alternating ceiling at 261 layers and the concurrent-operator nest at 669; those are [#201](https://github.com/karlssberg/Motiv/issues/201) and #145's own residual 2 respectively. This ticket is about size, not depth.
title: MaxEvaluationSize still bounds one fold on the asynchronous driver

Today `smith` writes `spec.md` and `plan.md`, builds against them, and leaves the evidence. The `implement` skill says a human approves `plan.md`, which is why it is a repository document, but when the writer of the contract and its executor are one agent the spec becomes a description of what was built rather than a contract for it, and `warden`'s "spec compliance first" loses its anchor. Planning also reads widely (policies, the ledger, follow-up) while building reads narrowly, and today both sit in one context. #30 showed what an act with no owner does: the nearest agent takes it.

**The fourth agent, named for what it does like the others.** `framer` frames: it sets the frame `smith` fills, `warden` checks the work against, and `sealer` (#30) stamps.

| | framer | smith | warden · sealer · scribe |
|---|---|---|---|
| writes | spec · plan · questions | code, tests, overview · changelog · evidence-todo | round records · the seal · migration facts |
| reads | `docs/` policies, the ledger, follow-up, the ticket | spec · plan | code and spec |

**The flow, and where a person is in it.** Routing is asked once at the start, as today. The framer phase is the interactive one: the person reads, objects, the framer revises, until the frame is right. Spawning `smith` is the approval; from there to the pull request the chain runs unattended, as it does now. `plan.md` records the moment with an `Approved <date> by <who>` line, the same shape as `routing.md`'s `Answered` line, because nothing else tells a later session or CI that a person saw the plan.

**Done when**

- `agents/framer.md` exists; the `feature-planner` and `confidence-check` skills move from `smith`'s design gate to it.
- `framer` runs only where the SDD ladder already calls for a `spec.md`; below that threshold `smith` alone, as today.
- `plan.md` gains the approval line, written when `smith` is spawned.
- Optional, and only if the owner wants the record: a `Planning` row in `routing.md` (`framer` · `the session`), noticed once when declared but not spawned, the way the smith mark works. Without it framer still runs; only "who framed this" goes unrecorded.
- `session-cost` reports time per agent from the subagent transcripts, so "smith is the short part" becomes a number. The one measurement on record is #30's 28-minute smith run, half of it the full suite the sealer now owns.

Not in docs/one-root-by-lifetime.md (PR #77, on release/v0.4.0 once merged); the design is this issue. Follows #30 (the sealer) so the four agents land as a set.
title: feat: the smith writes the contract it then executes — framer, the agent that frames the work

## Summary

Several TraceQL pipeline stages are evaluated in our own process after rows have already been read and transported. They could be compiled into the SQL we send. The clearest case is the spanset aggregate: `PlannedAggregate` is consumed only in `crates/pulsus-read/src/traces/search_eval.rs` and no code path generates SQL for it.

So for

```
{ .service.namespace = "prod" } | max(duration) > 1s
```

the filter is pushed down and prunes, then **every matching span is transported to us**, held in memory, grouped by trace, and most of it discarded. The database could have done that with `GROUP BY trace_id HAVING max(duration_ns) > 1000000000` and sent back only the traces that qualify.

This is not a limitation of the storage engine. `GROUP BY trace_id` is already used elsewhere in this codebase — in the search path and in the service-graph SQL.

## Why it matters more than latency

Compute is a fixed cost in a cloud deployment; cross-zone bandwidth is metered and variable. Bytes read from local disk into the database are close to free. **Bytes crossing between processes are a recurring charge**, so a stage that transports rows in order to discard them is paid for on every query.

There are three hops to count, not one:

```
client <-- pulsus-server <-- database <-- parts
                  ^              ^
                  |              +-- database to database: distributed fan-out, shard to coordinator
                  +----------------- metered in most topologies
```

A distributed `GROUP BY` sends partial aggregation state between shards rather than raw rows, so pushing an aggregate down shrinks the second hop as well as the first.

## What is evaluated where today

Pushed down: attribute equality, attribute regular expressions, physical columns, the time window, scope predicates.

Evaluated in our process: spanset aggregates, structural operators (descendant, child-of), cross-attribute comparisons, non-total arithmetic, `by()` regrouping.

That list needs splitting into three groups, because they need different answers:

1. **Cannot be pushed.** A structural operator needs the trace assembled; a cross-attribute comparison compares values stored on different rows.
2. **Could be pushed, and nobody has.** The aggregate case, where the filter is fully pushable and the aggregate reads a physical column.
3. **Pushed already, but prunes nothing.** An attribute regular expression compiles to a value match and still scans. Being pushed down and being cheap are separate claims.

## Waves

**Wave 1 — the inventory.** Every predicate and stage evaluated in our process, classified into the three groups above, with the SQL shape for group 2 and a measurement for group 3. Ranked by bytes saved on the metered hops.

**Waves 2 onward — one per pushable class**, in the order wave 1 establishes. Spanset aggregates are the expected first, since they have no SQL path at all.

## A decision this carries, to be settled before wave 2

Our result-size limits are enforced in our process and answer `422`. If the database performs the aggregation, a breach is detected somewhere else, and the limit has to move into the SQL or apply to a smaller result. The reference handles the same situation by returning a partial answer with a marker rather than refusing — and our responses carry no field for saying "incomplete". Whether we follow that or keep refusing is a separate decision and belongs in this issue, not in a wave.

## Not in scope

Rewriting anything in group 1. Changing what the queries mean. This issue is about where the same answer is computed.
title: TraceQL + LogQL: the shared engine that compiles a query pipeline to SQL, built on TraceQL first

The product is still in test mode with only part of the future manager/source pool connected. Immediate goal: remove software/state/routing/notification/dialogue defects and simplify the architecture so adding managers and traffic later does not multiply edge cases.

## Autopilot rules
- Prioritize real live conversations, handoffs and user requests over commit history.
- Confirm a defect from evidence where possible; otherwise add diagnostics/tests first.
- Safe reversible flow: branch → PR → required CI → merge only when green → verify production SHA, migrations, smoke/health and relevant live behavior.
- Do not make unrelated changes or edit other AnyTour projects from this roadmap.
- Do not silently enable off-shift managers, auto-assign conversations or add aggressive SLA escalation during test mode.
- Stop only for irreversible/high-risk decisions, missing secrets/credentials or unresolved product decisions.
